title: Theodore Roosevelt to John Hay, coded telegram of 27 May 1903 (Library of Congress, Roosevelt Papers reel 413 frame 0026): the State Department Red Cipher of 1876, read by William Echols

steps.what: The contributor transcribed the typed telegram from the Library of Congress scan; the project did not see the scan.

The contributor identified the 1876 State Department Red Cipher as the key, using a clue from Florentijn van Kampen's study for the group 10000, and read the 23 groups and the spelled letters (K I E L) from its pages.
Project check: 23 groups (22 distinct) each have an entry in key_excerpt.tsv and the replaced text is a coherent English telegram (VERIFICATION.md). No scan or codebook page compared.

validation.notes: A codebook lookup with 22 distinct groups; the coherence of the decoded sentences is the evidence, and no n-gram test applies.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The key is an existing codebook (the 1876 State Department Red Cipher) that had not been connected with this telegram; the contributor identified it and applied it. The project did not see the codebook pages and checked only that the result is coherent.

texts.label: Telegram of 27 May 1903, Roosevelt to Hay (LoC Roosevelt Papers reel 413 frame 0026)
texts.summary: Roosevelt, asks the Secretary of State what the object of the British government's request is, says he does not think it desirable that the trip should be made a junketing one, and says that if they touch at an English port it should be after the trip to Kiel, in his judgment.

reading_review.note: Read the decipherment as English sentences: the 23 groups replaced by their entries build a coherent telegram; the transcription and the codebook entries are the contributor's and were not compared with the images.

prior.where: The Roosevelt Center record gives no decoding and the contributor found none; the codebook is an archived key (NARA T1171; a repository note says it is printed in Weber 1979, not consulted here) not previously connected with this telegram.

human: William Echols submitted the transcription, the key identification and the reading (issue #353), made with GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex. The project checked the submission for internal coherence; it has not seen the scan or the codebook pages.
